text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
FRONT PAGE POLITICAL STORIES
GAZETA WYBORCZA

- Poland is ready to increase duty free import quotas for Swedish-made trucks if Sweden agrees to convert part of the Polish debt into environment related investments, Poland's Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz said during his visit to Stockholm yesterday.
- Two men set fire to the offices of the ex-communist Social Democratic Party's youth organisation (FM SDRP) yesterday. No one was hurt.
ECONOMIC AND MARKET STORIES
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- A business study group representing Thailand's textile, jewellery, and household durable industries will visit Poland this week to examine business opportunities in the country, Thailand's commercial counsellor Adisai Dhummakupt said.

- Central and east European countries are facing a long-term boom in the housing construction sector which will attract western construction firms and financial institutions, the presdient of the European housing loan office association FEECL Paul Oppitz said.
- Poland's Export Credit Insurance Corporation (KUKE) has launched simplified procedures of policy purchasing for small and medium size exporters.
DZIENNIK PRAWA I GOSPODARKI
- Bank Handlowy hopes to attract stable institutional investors to boost the bank's future share market price, BH's president Cezary Stypulkowski said.

- Poland's current account deficit reached $1.5 billion in the first quarter of 1997, the National Bank of Poland (NBP), the central bank, said. The account's balance was positive in the same period last year, NBP said.
- Poland's average monthly salary was 1,003 zlotys in the first quarter of 1997, the Central Statistical Office (GUS) said.
- Over 600 publishers from Poland and abroad will exhibit their offer at the 42 International Book Fair which starts in Warsaw tomorrow.

- The privately-owned El-Net telecoms operator will invest up to 150 million zlotys in developing a network to serve 150,000 customers in the Bydgoszcz province in the next four years, the company said.
- Around 100 wood-processing equipment firms from six countries are exhibiting their products at the Fourth International Forestry Fair in Warsaw underway this week.

- Around 20 million tourists visited Poland last year, which placed it in the group of the world's fifteen countries reporting highest tourist revenues in 1997, a report by the World Tourism Organisation (WTO) said.

- The European Commission's PHARE programme will grant 13 million Ecus for the Struder-2 development scheme for underdeveloped regions, which will cover the provinces of Lomza, Zamosc, Koszalin and Elblag.
GAZETA WYBORCZA
- The Pia Piasecki construction firm in Kielce, southern Poland, plans to enter the Warsaw bourse's parallel market in 1998, the company's supervisory board president Andrzej Piasecki said.
PARKIET

- Poland's Supreme Court has ruled against the Energoapartura electrical equipment maker's B-series share issue for formal reasons. "I can see no substantial arguments in favour of the ruling", the Polish Securities Commission (KPW) president Jacek Socha said.
-- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
